teams.heading: Fiji beat Italy 21-16 in Udine for first Nations Championship win
teams.body: The 21-16 result in Round 6 closed both sides' pool campaigns at Udine's Bluenergy Stadium, and Jake White's side had arrived without a Nations Championship victory after fading in the second half of a 43-15 defeat by Ireland. Italy were weakened late: OnRugby reported tighthead Simone Ferrari suffered a left upper-limb injury an hour before kickoff, with Marco Riccioni promoted to start and Ion Neculai added to the bench.

lead.why: Every NEW item failed the test: #1 is the Latui rout already run today with no new development, #2 is Ireland's story of the same match, and #3 is Italy's injury story.

teams.heading: Slade opens scoring as England beat All Blacks by record margin
teams.body: Fin Smith's grubber put Henry Slade over after four minutes at Allianz Stadium. Jack van Poortvliet and Ben Earl added first-half tries as England led 19-0 after 36 minutes, and Ollie Chessum crashed over for the fourth soon after the restart. The 37-12 result, five tries to two, was England's biggest winning margin over New Zealand, eclipsing 2012's 38-21, Planet Rugby noted. The Guardian added that it came despite Tommy Freeman's pre-game injury withdrawal.

lead.why: The record 37-12 win over the All Blacks is the day's biggest England event, and neither the Moody haka nor Borthwick's referee comments are fresh leads.

teams.heading: French federation's Argentina-match tribute to Federico Martin Aramburu enlists Antoine Dupont
teams.body: Aramburu's son was named to walk out before France-Argentina in an Argentina jersey, holding the hands of both captains, Dupont and hooker Julián Montoya, in honour of his dual nationality, Rugbyrama reported. The former Argentine player, well known in the French championship in the early 2000s, was murdered in Paris in 2022 by two far-right activists. They were later jailed for 26 and 19 years. The federation also scheduled a minute's applause in his memory at Saint-Denis.

teams.heading: McCarthy and Ryan score twice as Ireland XV rout Fiji Latui
teams.body: Ireland's second string, the Ireland XV, met little resistance at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Friday night as Fiji Latui collected four yellow cards and a red card in the first half, at one point dropping to 12 men. Captain Gus McCarthy and Connacht's Daniel Ryan crossed twice apiece in a nine-try win, while Joey Carbery set up Ryan's opener and dived under the posts for one of his own. Paul Boyle withdrew from the bench with a neck issue; Scott Penny replaced him.

lead.why: The Springboks win has already run, and the Ireland XV's rout of Fiji Latui is the only new men's 15s Ireland event.

teams.heading: Quesada handed Miotti his debut at fly-half before Italy's Fiji defeat
teams.body: Wing injuries to Lynagh, Faissal, Pani and Trulla shaped the call, Quesada explained before Saturday's 16-21 loss to Fiji in Udine. Ange Capuozzo moved to the wing and Tommaso Allan to full-back so Domingo Miotti could debut at No. 10. Quesada denied it was a snub of Paolo Garbisi, who knew Miotti would come in after the previous two tests. He also said a debut in a key position is easier from the start. Alessandro Ortombina replaced Federico Ruzza as lineout leader.

lead.why: NEW item #1, Ferrari's pre-match injury, already ran today and the pack reports no new development, so Quesada's selection reasoning is the strongest unreported Italy story.

teams.heading: Liam McConnell scores hat-trick on third Scotland appearance in Japan rout
teams.body: The 22-year-old Edinburgh back-rower was the standout of Saturday's 11-try, 67-5 win at Murrayfield, and BBC Scotland chief sports writer Tom English called him electrifying in attack and defence alike. English noted the long-running frustration among McConnell's backers at his lack of Scotland opportunities. His second try came early in the second half from Darcy Graham's kick through, chase and offload. Graham's own hat-trick took his international try tally to 41.

lead.why: A rookie's hat-trick in only his third Test is fresh, Scotland-centric news that the earlier Townsend edition did not cover.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy rotated Wales for Wallabies after 300 tackles against All Blacks
teams.body: Wales went into Saturday's Nations Championship test against Australia in Cardiff with a changed side. Tandy cited the 300 tackles and high ball-in-play time of the New Zealand win. Sam Costelow and Tomos Williams formed the half-back pairing, Blair Murray started at full-back and Dewi Lake captained the side, while Joe Hawkins and Louie Hennessey were named among the replacements. Tandy said: "The guys played outstanding against the All Blacks but we’ve got guys who are fresh and hungry."

lead.why: Tandy's selection and stated reason for rotating after the All Blacks win is the freshest hard Wales team news in the coverage.

teams.heading: Rugbyrama flags flaws France knew in Shaun Edwards' Pumas defensive system
teams.body: Before Saturday's Nations Championship meeting at the Stade de France, Midi Olympique's Nicolas Zanardi argued that six years under Edwards, now in charge of the Pumas' defence, left Les Bleus fluent in his demands: a 13-man front line, double tackles to kill offloads and no easy ruck ball. He cited weak points France had felt first-hand, notably forwards left to fend for themselves after lineouts, and asked whether Tomás Albornoz would be targeted. France lineout coach Laurent Sempéré said Edwards had surely evolved too, adapting to his new colleagues.

lead.why: The freshest item about Argentina itself, on how France read Shaun Edwards' Pumas defence, since the tribute story has already run.

teams.heading: Les Kiss left Fraser McReight on the bench for Wales test
teams.body: Carlo Tizzano got the nod in a back row captained by Harry Wilson alongside Rob Valetini as Australia faced Wales at the Principality Stadium on Saturday night. Carter Gordon and Ryan Lonergan formed the halves, with Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Len Ikitau in midfield. Kiss's bench ran five forwards to three backs, McReight joined by Billy Pollard, Angus Bell, Allan Alaalatoa and Jeremy Williams. Frenchman Luc Ramos took the whistle.

lead.why: Both Wright items have already run, and this is the only remaining item in the coverage that prints Australia's selection for Cardiff.

teams.heading: Harada hip drop and Stolberg tackle bring Japan two Murrayfield yellows
teams.body: Both offences came from replacements in the closing quarter of Saturday's 67-5 defeat by Scotland. Mamoru Harada was sin-binned in the 69th minute for a hip-drop tackle, and Michael Stolberg followed in the 79th for an early tackle, Planet Rugby reported. Scotland's 11 tries included hat-tricks for Liam McConnell and Darcy Graham. Japan's only reply was Takuro Matsunaga's unconverted 53rd-minute try, scored after a box kick bounced awkwardly and eluded Kyle Rowe.

lead.why: The fifth-place angle on the result has already run, so the discipline in the same defeat is the fresh Japan story.

teams.heading: All Blacks slump to record 37-12 defeat by England at Twickenham
teams.body: Dave Rennie's side were beaten by 25 points at Allianz Stadium on Saturday, eclipsing England's previous best margin in the fixture — 38-21 in 2012 — and handing them successive wins over New Zealand for the first time since 2002 and 2003. Ethan de Groot and Beauden Barrett, in his 150th Test, scored the tries. According to SA Rugby Magazine, the result leaves the Springboks needing one log point against Ireland in Dublin to top the southern hemisphere standings and claim a place in the final.

lead.why: The record defeat is the day's most widely reported New Zealand event, and earlier editions only covered reaction to it.

teams.heading: Springboks beaten 20-17 by Ireland in Dublin without banned Rassie Erasmus
teams.body: Saturday's final-round Nations Championship Test at the Aviva Stadium, refereed by Christophe Ridley, followed defeat in France a week earlier, so a side that won their first four rounds finished with two straight losses. Erasmus was absent, serving a six-match World Rugby ban, and SA Rugby have requested a full misconduct hearing. Nick Mallett had told the Talking Boks podcast that the absence would have no detrimental effect on the squad's motivation. South Africa go into Sunday third of 12 on the log.

lead.why: The Dublin result is the day's hard event for South Africa, distinct from the watchalong story already run.
